summary: Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer works in religious studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower, completed postdoctoral mentorship under Xiuping Hong, and held a post at the University of Pittsburgh.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya (1933–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, later serving as researcher and Central Asian manuscript curator there.
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and also studied under Karin Preisendanz.

Margherita Trento works in Indology and history/archaeology. She was affiliated with the CNRS (attested 2021), served on the editorial board of Studies on the History of Śaivism (attested 2021), and became an associate professor at EHESS (attested 2025).

Marguerite E. Adiceam (1911–1989) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon under Jean Filliozat. She taught at the Lycée Français de Pondichéry (1946–1954) and was a scientific member at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1966–1971).

Marguerite Lobsiger-Dellenbach (1905–1993) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning a PhD at the University of Geneva in 1935, she served as vice-director (1947) and director (1952–1967) of the Musée d'ethnographie de Genève, succeeding Eugène Pittard.

Maria Carlotta Avanzi specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She earned degrees from the University of Turin and a doctorate from Kyoto University (2018–2024), holding posts at Akita Prefectural University (2021) and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Maria Elisabeth Lulius van Goor (1866–1929) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Leiden University under Jacob Samuel Speyer, earning a PhD in 1915. She held an attachée post at EFEO (1922–1923) and was Praeceptor of Pāli at Leiden in 1924.

Maria Gallas specializes in philosophy and Indology. She earned a master's degree in philosophy from the National University of Distance Education (2019–2022) and is a PhD student at the Universidad a Distancia de Madrid.

Maria Heim works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Reed College and Harvard University (PhD under Charles Hallisey), she also studied with Jambuvijaya, W. S. Karunatillake, and Nagin J. Shah, and served as Associate Professor at Amherst College.

Maria Vasylieva specializes in Buddhist studies. She holds degrees from Uppsala University, the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and the International Buddhist College. In 2020, she became an assistant professor at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Maria Wilkins Smith (1884–1973) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied at Bryn Mawr College and earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Roland Grubb Kent in 1929, before teaching Latin at Temple University.

Marian Ury (1932–1995) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and served as professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at the University of California, Davis (1969–1995).

Marianne Oort works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University under Michael Witzel and F. B. J. Kuiper, and served as an assistant librarian at Leiden University from 1978 to 1997.

Marianne Pieper (born 1949) completed her habilitation at Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. She taught at the University of Kassel (1994–1996) and served as a professor of sociology at the University of Hamburg from 1996 to 2015.

Marianne Winder (1918–2001) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying at London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Llewellyn Snellgrove. Her career included posts at Nottingham, the University of London, and the Wellcome Trust as curator and consultant.

Marianne Yaldiz is a scholar of history, archaeology, Central Asian, and Indological studies. She served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (attested 1997–2005) and Direktorin of the Museum für Indische Kunst (attested 2006).

Mariano José Saldanha (1878–1975) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sebastião Rodolfo Dalgado. He taught at Liceu Nacional Afonso de Albuquerque (1915–1929), the University of Lisbon (1929–1946), and was Subdirector at ISCSP (1929–1948).

Mariano Rampolla del Tindaro (1893–1945) was an Indologist who studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University and under Oreste Nazari. In 1933, he was appointed professor of Indian religious history and Sanskrit at the Pontifical Urban University.
Marie Brožová was a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. She studied at Charles University, completing her PhD under the supervision of Josef Zubatý in 1921.
